title: RainPro-8: An Efficient Deep Learning Model to Estimate Rainfall Probabilities Over 8 Hours
claim: A compact multi-resolution network fuses sources at several scales and decodes all lead times jointly, keeping parameter count and compute low.
layout: 4 colour-coded horizontal bands (4/8/16 km plus a 2 km output panel), left-to-right data flow with up/down-sampling arrows between bands, tensor channel counts in boxes
description: A block diagram of a multi-scale encoder-decoder. Three horizontal bands are shaded blue (4 km), green (8 km) and yellow (16 km). A fourth purple panel at the lower right shows the 2 km output. Each band has input source tensors drawn as tall rounded rectangles with channel counts (256, 192, 96). Arrows lead through labelled operations: Stack & Embed, Merge, Center crop, Concat, 2x ResNet and 12x MaxViT blocks. Downsample arrows go down from one band to the next. Upsample arrows go back up along the right side. The blue top band ends in a 128-channel tensor. That tensor feeds a final layer that produces a row of 256-channel output maps, labelled T+10m through T+8h. A rounded box at the bottom gives the output tensor shape and the conditional exceedance-probability formula. The eye goes first to the coloured bands and the arrow flow.
caption: RainPro-8 architecture, optimized for reduced parameter count and efficiency, integrating multiple data sources of varying resolution for simultaneous prediction of all lead times.
abstract: We present a deep learning model for high-resolution probabilistic precipitation forecasting over an 8-hour horizon in Europe, overcoming the limitations of radar-only deep learning models with short forecast lead times. Our model efficiently integrates multiple data sources - including radar, satellite, and physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) - while capturing long-range interactions, resulting in accurate forecasts with robust uncertainty quantification through consistent probabilistic maps. Featuring a compact architecture, it enables more efficient training and faster inference than existing models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our model surpasses current operational NWP systems, extrapolation-based methods, and deep-learning nowcasting models, setting a new standard for high-resolution precipitation forecasting in Europe, ensuring a balance between accuracy, interpretability, and computational efficiency.
